lead: This unit puts a message on the amplitude of a carrier and takes it off again. It works out the AM spectrum and power, removes the carrier (DSB-SC) and one sideband (SSB, VSB), builds the modulators and detectors, places them in transmitters and the superheterodyne receiver, and shares one channel among many messages by FDM. After it you can calculate modulation index, power, bandwidth, detector time constants, image frequency and image rejection.
about: The unit starts with conventional AM: the modulation index, the three-line spectrum and the power split between carrier and sidebands. It then removes the carrier (DSB-SC, with coherent detection and carrier recovery) and one sideband (SSB and VSB). The next two chapters turn the mathematics into circuits: square-law, balanced and ring modulators, then envelope and coherent detectors. The last three place these circuits in systems: low-level and high-level transmitters, the superheterodyne receiver, and frequency division multiplexing, which stacks many SSB channels on one link.

chapters.idea: AM multiplies a carrier by (1 + m cos ω_m t); the modulation index sets sideband size, bandwidth and extra power.
chapters.depth: Cover s(t) = A_c[1 + m cos(2πf_m t)] cos(2πf_c t). Define carrier amplitude A_c in volts, modulating amplitude A_m in volts, modulation index m = A_m/A_c, and percentage modulation. Show the line spectrum at f_c and f_c ± f_m, bandwidth 2f_m for a tone, and overmodulation when m > 1. Give P_c = V_c²/(2R), P_total = P_c(1 + m²/2), each sideband power m²P_c/4, and efficiency m²/(2 + m²). Mention the current form I_t = I_c√(1 + m²/2). Some syllabi call this conventional AM or linear CW modulation. Keep multitone AM to a short note.

figure.title: AM line spectrum
figure.aria: Line spectrum with a 10 V carrier at 1000 kHz and two 2 V sidebands at 999 kHz and 1001 kHz.

chapters.example: A 10 V carrier at 1 MHz is amplitude-modulated by a 1 kHz tone of amplitude 4 V across a 50 Ω load. Find m, the sideband amplitudes, the bandwidth, the carrier power, the total power and the efficiency.
chapters.trap: Forgetting that m > 1 folds the envelope and creates extra sidebands in a real modulator; the formula P_total = P_c(1 + m²/2) is for a single tone with m ≤ 1.
chapters.prereq: Unit 1: Fourier transform, band-pass signals, carrier and sideband ideas.
chapters.leave: Noise performance and figure of merit go to Unit 3; angle modulation is a separate scheme.

chapters.idea: DSB-SC transmits only the two sidebands; a coherent detector multiplies by a synchronized carrier and low-pass filters.
chapters.depth: Write s(t) = A_c m(t) cos(2πf_c t). Show that the spectrum has no line at f_c and occupies f_c ± W for message bandwidth W. Explain coherent detection: multiply by cos(2πf_c t), low-pass filter, and get (A_c/2)m(t). Add phase error φ: output scales by cos φ; a 90° error gives zero and a small frequency error gives a beat. Mention carrier recovery by a pilot or Costas loop only at block level. Some syllabi call this DSB/SC or double-sideband suppressed carrier.

figure.title: Coherent DSB-SC detector
figure.aria: The received DSB-SC signal and a local carrier enter a product device; a low-pass filter then gives the baseband output.

chapters.example: A 2 V, 1 kHz tone modulates a 10 V, 100 kHz carrier in DSB-SC. Write the two sideband terms. Find the output after coherent detection with a local carrier of amplitude 1 V and zero phase error.
chapters.trap: A phase error φ gives a cos φ loss; a 90° error gives zero, and a frequency error gives a beating audio tone. Coherent detection is not an envelope detector.
chapters.prereq: Chapter 2.1 AM spectrum; Unit 1 Fourier transform and multiplication.
chapters.leave: SSB/VSB bandwidth saving to 2.3; carrier recovery circuits beyond a block mention.

chapters.idea: SSB sends one sideband, halving bandwidth; VSB sends one sideband plus a small vestige to make filtering practical.
chapters.depth: For SSB, show upper-sideband and lower-sideband spectra, bandwidth W, and coherent detection. Name filter method, phase-shift method and Weaver method; explain that the phase-shift method uses a Hilbert transform π/2 shift from Unit 1. For VSB, show a filter that passes one sideband fully and a vestige of the other near the carrier; bandwidth is W + f_v, where f_v is the vestige width. State that analog TV video is the standard VSB example. Some syllabi call SSB single-sideband suppressed carrier. Keep filter design qualitative.

figure.title: SSB or VSB by filtering
figure.aria: A product modulator shifts a 0-3 kHz audio band to 100 kHz; the band-pass filter keeps one sideband and, for VSB, a 0.5 kHz vestige.

chapters.example: A 0-3 kHz audio band modulates a 100 kHz carrier. Compare DSB, SSB and VSB bandwidths if the VSB filter keeps a 0.5 kHz vestige.
chapters.trap: SSB does not mean any one sideband without saying which; the filter must reject the other by enough decibels. VSB bandwidth is not W; it is W plus the vestige width.
chapters.prereq: Chapter 2.2 DSB-SC and coherent detection; Unit 1 Hilbert transform and complex envelope.
chapters.leave: Practical crystal filter design and TV receiver details to later; FM stereo multiplexing to Unit 3.

chapters.idea: Nonlinear devices multiply carrier and message; square-law gives AM with carrier, balanced connection cancels the carrier.
chapters.depth: Use i = a0 + a1v + a2v². Put v = A_c cos ω_c t + A_m cos ω_m t. Expand: the linear term gives the carrier at ω_c; the square term gives sidebands at ω_c ± ω_m plus DC, second harmonic and message square. A band-pass filter selects the AM. In a balanced modulator, two matched devices with opposite inputs cancel carrier and message, leaving DSB-SC sidebands. Mention the ring modulator as a diode balanced version. Some syllabi call this the nonlinear method. State that the linear collector modulator belongs with transmitters in 2.6.

figure.title: Square-law AM generator
figure.aria: A 2 V carrier and a 0.5 V tone are added and passed through a square-law device; a band-pass filter selects the AM output.

chapters.example: In a square-law device i = 1.0v + 0.2v² (A/V and A/V²), v = 2 cos(2π100k t) + 0.5 cos(2π1k t) V. Find the carrier and sideband current amplitudes at the output filter and the modulation index.
chapters.trap: The square-law term does not create the carrier at ω_c; the linear term does. A balanced modulator cancels the carrier only if the two halves are matched; mismatch leaves carrier leakage.
chapters.prereq: Chapter 2.1 AM expression and spectrum; basic diode or transistor nonlinearity.
chapters.leave: Collector modulator and power amplifiers to 2.6; detailed bias design not needed.

chapters.idea: An envelope detector follows the AM envelope with a diode and RC filter; a coherent detector multiplies by a local carrier and works even without a carrier.
chapters.depth: For the envelope detector, show diode, RC load and DC block. Give the design inequality 1/(2πf_c) ≪ RC ≪ 1/(2πW), where W is the highest modulating frequency. Explain diagonal clipping when RC is too large and carrier ripple when RC is too small. The envelope is A_c[1 + m(t)]; overmodulation cannot be recovered simply. For coherent detection of AM, multiply by a local carrier and low-pass filter to get (A_c/2)[1 + m(t)]. Compare cost, synchronization and use with DSB-SC/SSB.

figure.title: Envelope detector
figure.aria: An AM input passes through a diode and a 10 µs RC filter; a DC block removes the average and leaves the audio output.

chapters.example: An AM wave 10[1 + 0.5 cos(2π1000t)] cos(2π100000t) V is detected by an envelope detector. Find the envelope, the audio output after DC blocking, and a suitable RC range.
chapters.trap: RC too large causes diagonal clipping on fast falls; RC too small leaves carrier ripple. Overmodulation with m > 1 cannot be recovered by a simple envelope detector.
chapters.prereq: Chapter 2.1 AM; Chapter 2.2 coherent detection; Unit 1 low-pass filters.
chapters.leave: FM detectors and noise in detectors to Unit 3; AGC and receiver details to 2.7.

chapters.idea: Low-level transmitters modulate at low power and then amplify linearly; high-level transmitters modulate the final RF stage at full power.
chapters.depth: Draw the low-level chain: RF oscillator, buffer, low-level modulator, linear class B RF amplifier, antenna. Draw the high-level chain: oscillator and buffer, RF driver, class C final amplifier, high-level modulator such as a collector modulator feeding the final stage. Compare linearity, efficiency, power handling, adjustment and typical use. Use the power relations from 2.1. Explain that a class C stage after a low-level modulator would distort AM, while a high-level collector modulator varies the supply of a class C stage.

figure.title: Low-level AM transmitter
figure.aria: An RF oscillator feeds a buffer and a low-level modulator, which also takes audio input; a linear power amplifier then drives the antenna.

chapters.example: A 1 kW carrier is amplitude-modulated with m = 0.5. Find the total power and total sideband power. A low-level modulator produces 2 W; a following linear amplifier has 20 dB gain. Find the final carrier power.
chapters.trap: Do not use a class C amplifier after a low-level modulator: it is nonlinear and will distort AM. High-level modulation can use a class C final stage because modulation is applied to its supply.
chapters.leave: Receiver sensitivity and AGC to 2.7; FM transmitters to Unit 3.

chapters.idea: A superheterodyne receiver translates every incoming RF to a fixed intermediate frequency, where filtering and amplification are easy.
chapters.depth: Cover antenna, RF amplifier, mixer, local oscillator, IF amplifier and filter, detector, audio amplifier and AGC. Define IF, high-side injection f_LO = f_RF + f_IF, low-side injection f_LO = f_RF − f_IF, and image frequency f_image = f_RF + 2f_IF for high-side injection. Explain image rejection by the RF filter before the mixer. State typical AM broadcast IF as 455 kHz. Keep tracking and alignment qualitative. Some syllabi call this the superhet receiver.

figure.title: Superheterodyne receiver
figure.aria: The antenna signal passes through an RF amplifier to a mixer, where a local oscillator shifts it to a fixed IF; IF amplification, detection and audio output follow.

chapters.example: An AM broadcast receiver has an RF signal at 1.000 MHz and an IF of 455 kHz with high-side injection. Find the local oscillator frequency and the image frequency. If the RF filter passband is 20 kHz wide around 1.000 MHz, does it reject the image?
chapters.trap: The image frequency is not the local oscillator; for high-side injection f_image = f_RF + 2f_IF. Low-side injection gives f_LO = f_RF − f_IF and a different image.
chapters.prereq: Chapter 2.5 detectors; Unit 1 frequency translation and band-pass filters.
chapters.leave: Noise figure and receiver sensitivity to Unit 3; FM receiver, ratio detector and stereo to Unit 3.

chapters.idea: FDM gives each message a different frequency slot; filters combine them at the transmitter and separate them at the receiver.
chapters.depth: Explain shifting each baseband signal by a different carrier, usually with SSB for voice, then summing. Define slot width and guard band. Show a four-channel example at 60, 64, 68 and 72 kHz, with 4 kHz slots and 3.1 kHz voice bandwidth. Give the composite bandwidth as N times slot width. Mention crosstalk from filter leakage and imperfect guard bands. Name telephony groups and broadcast use, but keep hierarchy brief. Some syllabi call it frequency-division multiplexing or frequency-division multiple access.

figure.title: Four-channel FDM
figure.aria: Four SSB channels at 60-64, 64-68, 68-72 and 72-76 kHz are added by a summer to form one composite FDM signal.

chapters.example: Four voice channels, each 3.1 kHz wide, use FDM with 4 kHz slots starting at 60 kHz. Find each channel's band, the guard band, and the total composite bandwidth.
chapters.trap: The guard band is not signal bandwidth; total FDM bandwidth is N times slot width, not N times voice bandwidth. Filter leakage causes crosstalk.
chapters.prereq: Chapter 2.3 SSB; Chapter 2.7 receiver frequency translation; Unit 1 spectra.
chapters.leave: TDM to Unit 4; OFDM and multiple access to Unit 6.
